headline: Revenue climbs as GAAP earnings dip on non-cash items
summary_short: Enbridge reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $29.32B CAD, up 97.1% y/y, while GAAP EPS fell 36.0% y/y to $0.64 CAD; the company reaffirmed 2026 guidance and grew its secured project backlog to $41B.
summary_long: Revenue rose 31.1% q/q and 97.1% y/y to $29.32B CAD, while GAAP EPS fell 16.9% q/q and 36.0% y/y to $0.64 CAD as net income of $1.50B CAD (-15.6% q/q, -34.1% y/y) absorbed non-cash derivative fair-value losses, a note-exchange hedge charge and a crude-oil inventory adjustment, partly offset by the absence of last year's Ohio impairment. Operating income was $2.91B CAD (-9.8% q/q, +27.1% y/y). Adjusted EBITDA and distributable cash flow grew on higher Gas Transmission and Distribution rate-case revenue. Enbridge reaffirmed its full-year adjusted EBITDA ($20.2-20.8B CAD) and DCF-per-share ($5.70-6.10 CAD) guidance and grew its secured capital backlog to $41B after sanctioning the Line 5 Relocation project.
confidence_notes: All figures are in Canadian dollars, Enbridge's reporting currency. The Revenue KPI is the XBRL 'Revenues' tag, which for Enbridge includes commodity costs passed through in Gas Distribution and trading operations and can swing materially q/q and y/y independent of EBITDA; the release does not discuss this line item, so no driver is attributed to it beyond the SEC-verbatim figure.

drivers.explanation: Non-cash unrealized changes in derivative values hedging FX, interest-rate and commodity risk, plus a note-exchange hedge loss and a crude-oil inventory adjustment, partly offset by the absence of last year's Ohio rate-asset impairment.
Same non-cash derivative, hedge-loss and inventory items that reduced net income were only partly offset by the absent Ohio impairment and steady underlying operating performance.
Adjusted EBITDA and distributable cash flow grew on higher rate-case revenue in Gas Transmission and Distribution, the secured growth backlog rose to $41B, and 2026 guidance was reaffirmed.
